children: Asian equities edged lower on Wednesday October 7 as an intraday drop in Japan's market outweighed gains in South Korea, and the region failed to follow the record-setting rally on Wall Street.

MSCI's gauge of Asia-Pacific shares lost 0.1% in early trade. South Korea's Kospi rose about 0.33%, while Japan's Nikkei 225 dropped 0.31% while the Topix slipped 0.043, The Hang Seng futures barely moved.
In India, the GIFT Nifty, which indicates how the country's stock market would open for the day predicted a negative start in the red.
In currencies, the Japanese yen weakened 0.2% to 158.42 per dollar, while the offshore yuan held steady at 6.7032.

Wall Street set the tone overnight as both the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq 100 closed at all-time highs amid the US earnings season that is set to commence next week. Gains in artificial intelligence stocks drove the advance, and Nvidia's market value moved close to $6 trillion.

Separately, Taiwan's Taiex index had beat the Kospi by 23 percentage points between July and September, which was the widest gap since the turn of the century. Taiwanese companies have also upgraded their earnings forecasts faster than Korean rivals for the first time since March 2025.
Technology stocks meanwhile continue to remain in focus after the Financial Times reported that SpaceX wants to raise $40 billion to buy Nvidia chips.
Global stocks were also hovering near record highs as investors seemed to expect companies to withstand higher interest rates and energy costs.

With few economic data releases due, traders were expected to look to the earnings season for evidence that the hundreds of billions of dollars tech giants are spending on AI is producing stronger profits a Bloomberg report noted. Macro traders were also keeping watch on elevated oil prices, multi-year highs in bond yields and swings in currency markets, the report said.

Crude rose in early Asian trading. Brent gained 0.8% to top $101 a barrel, as traders weighed higher flows through the Strait of Hormuz against a rise in Iranian attacks on vessels. West Texas Intermediate climbed 0.7% to $90.07 a barrel.

title: Asian stocks edge lower against Wall Street rally, Japan leads loses
